items.title: Cyclone Murasu: 8 dead, CM Naidu estimates damages at Rs 1919 cr in Andhra
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the aftermath of Cyclone Murasu on Thursday, November 5, inquiring with officials about damage caused across various departments, including Agriculture, Electricity, Municipal Administration and Panchayat Raj. Officials reported that a total of eight people had died due to the cyclone—five in Bapatla district, two in Guntur district and one in Palnadu district. According to a preliminary damage assessment, Cyclone Murasu has caused an estimated loss of Rs 1,918.55 crore to the state. Agricultural crops were damaged across 1,43,122 hectares, affecting 1,86,063 farmers. Horticultural crops suffered damage across 6,749 hectares, impacting 12,586 farmers. A total of 983 houses, 346 boats and 220 fishing nets were also damaged, officials told the CM. They said it would take another 48–72 hours to assess the extent of crop damage accurately after floodwaters receded. A week before Murasu, at least seven people were killed when Cyclone Arnab lashed the state, and a preliminary estimate of losses stood at Rs 4,600 crore. Allahabad High Court asks its administrative wing to examine plea to streamline caveats in criminal cases
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently indicated that its administrative side will examine a plea seeking the introduction of a system to streamline the filing, registration and notification of caveats in criminal proceedings [ Anupriya Agarwal vs State of UP and Another ]. A Division Bench of Justice Rajan Roy and Justice Manjive Shukla was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) petition that flagged a gap in the Allahabad Hon'ble Court Rules, 1952. The petition filed by advocate Anupriya Agarwal pointed out that these rules did not lay down any specific mechanism for filing, registering, processing or notifying caveats in criminal proceedings such as in bail applications, criminal appeals, etc. Caveat pleas are requests made to a court to hear a party before passing any order in a matter that may affect their interests. The Court observed that while the petition for a formal caveat filing system prima facie raises an important issue concerning access to justice, the subject matter essentially pertains to court procedure. The Facebook post is stated to have been shared by the petitioner on May 20, 2025. items.title: Unpaid traffic challans issued before October 2020 cannot be ground to deny vehicle registration: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has held that transport authorities cannot refuse to process applications relating to vehicle registration, merely because traffic challans issued before October 1, 2020, remain unpaid. [TN Kumar v Ministry of Road Transport and Highways & ors] Justice Murali Purushothaman held that Rule 167(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (Rules) as amended , which restricts certain vehicle-related services when traffic challans remain unpaid, cannot be applied to violations that occurred before the provision came into force. The Court explained that the rule introduced a restriction that did not previously exist and could therefore operate only from the date it came into force. It clarified that unless the law clearly provided otherwise, a new restriction could not be imposed on the basis of challans issued before the rule was introduced.
